content.prompt: I have built a primitive slide projector by shining light from a point source through a transparent slide held up 10 cm away. The light then falls onto a wall that is parallel to the slide and distant 1 metre from it.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a labelled diagram of a triangle on the slide and its image on the wall.

answer.short: A possible labelled diagram is shown.
answer.worked: Draw rays from the point light source through the triangle’s vertices on the slide to the corresponding image vertices on the parallel wall. Label the light-to-slide distance 10 cm and the slide-to-wall distance 1 m.

spec.description: An authored perspective projection diagram showing a point source, a triangle on a slide and its corresponding image on a parallel wall. The triangle shape is illustrative because the source specifies no triangle dimensions.
spec.mathematics: The slide and wall occupy parallel planes at distances 10 cm and 110 cm from O. Corresponding vertices lie on common rays from O, with image position vectors eleven times the original vectors.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete labelled construction appears only in answer editions.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What are the centre of enlargement and the enlargement factor of the transformation?

answer.short: Centre: the point light source. Enlargement factor: $11$.
answer.worked:
The centre is the point light source, since corresponding vertices lie on rays from it.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Light-to-wall distance}&=10+100\\&=110\text{ cm}\\k&=\frac{110}{10}\\k&=11\end{align*}$$
